lanes.why: Baseline is a stale 104-row identity-weak archive; no fresh pristine U0 over the current tree.
104 rows, weak target-name identity, no current per-row provenance; oracle joins on name (CD-003).
Historical observation only; not current qualification.

Classification: historical-dirty-tree-aggregate-smoke (label sidecar: docs/evidence/G3/u2s3-full-3/CLASSIFICATION.json). Archived run used a dirty 23-file staged tree (digest cc0d283a...); the current staged tree has 24 files and a different digest, and critical storage (cursor.rs, slate.rs, post_wal_guard.rs, storage.rs) changed after the run. Raw observation: 106 unique executable rows, 105 exited 0, 1 exited 101, 0 timeouts, 462 parsed passed, 2 parsed failed, 1 parsed ignored, 34 zero-case rows. That observation is preserved; it is NOT current-tree conformance and is never to be summarised as '105 green'.

The Rust remote-WAL client is incompatible with the current Worker protocol (C-P0-01): no capabilities, numeric u64 parsing, caller-supplied throughLsn, no batch envelope, legacy fencedBy expectations. Any prior U3.0 green claim is stale.
Product profiles fail closed; the v17 per-database classic|slatedb-r2 seam is being built as refusal-first (S-P0-06). No product E2E exists.
v17 requires official Rust/Python/TS driver suites on pristine and fork-classic now (post-G2 for slatedb-r2). Catalogue rows are in-repo wrappers only.

owner_decision_rule: An OPEN owner decision cannot support a green gate. OD-005 (flake expiry placeholders) is OPEN; therefore any policy verdict that leans on the flake ledger is a development comparison, not final conformance.
